machine_specs.summary: The transfer engine connects intent, reservation, ledger entry and confirmation. This notebook examines the documentary consistency of those boundaries without executing payments.

phases.name: Obligation and message inventory
phases.narrative: Obligation O-001 exists independently of messages M1 and M2. The inventory identifies producer, queue, consumer, ledger and status query. Each component declares which revision it retains and which result it can reconstruct after a restart. The transport ID tracks a delivery; it does not determine whether the business effect should be repeated.

phases.name: Authorization and approved content
phases.narrative: Authorization contains the subject, beneficiary, currency, amount and revision. An allowed case involving an authorized resource and a rejected case involving another organization’s resource are documented before funds are reserved. Changing the beneficiary invalidates earlier approval even when the amount stays the same. The consumer must not trust an approved label without verifying its associated revision.

phases.name: Interruption and retry
phases.narrative: The model is interrupted after the ledger entry and before confirmation. When another message arrives, the worker checks the durable obligation and returns the existing result. Evidence records that the second arrival creates no second entry. Any intermediate state must be resolved explicitly rather than by blindly repeating the original command.

phases.name: Reconciliation and compensation
phases.narrative: Review compares reservation, ledger entry and confirmation by obligation, currency and revision. A refund is a separate linked transition with its own idempotency and cumulative limit. The notebook distinguishes data correction, compensation of an effect and cancellation before execution. These operations do not automatically share the same authorization criterion.

phases.name: Closure and restrictions
phases.narrative: Acceptance retains an allowed, a rejected and a recovered operation. The fictional outcome documents one effect and any pending condition. No real processing times or financial guarantees are presented. A state capture is insufficient to close the case while any consumer remains unreconciled.

machine_specs.summary: Central identity represents sessions, refresh credentials and challenges. This notebook distinguishes a person or service from its devices and derived credentials.

phases.name: Access-family inventory
phases.narrative: The inventory lists a short-lived session, refresh credential, device, delegated mandate and operation challenge. All refer to a stable subject, but their validity periods and purposes differ. It records which component can issue a derivative and which retains revocation authority. No valid secrets or tokens are used.

phases.name: Binding the intent
phases.narrative: The challenge describes an exact intent rather than generic approval lasting several minutes. Changing currency, recipient or amount requires a new decision. A matching confirmation, a confirmation with different content and repeated consumption of the same challenge are documented. Expected outcomes do not depend on a device’s visible name.

phases.name: Revocation and consumers
phases.narrative: The model revokes the access family while a refresh is pending. Acceptance requires rejection of the session, the refresh and any delegation withdrawn by recovery policy. A consumer retaining stale permission remains pending even if the central catalog already shows removal.

phases.name: Account recovery
phases.narrative: Recovery changes who controls the account and requires reevaluation of support sessions. The notebook retains a legitimate help path without allowing a browser change to reset the attempt budget. Public messages are uniform, and technical details remain in a restricted scenario record.

phases.name: Closure and evidence of scope
phases.narrative: The final record identifies which derivatives were checked and which could not be verified. A token’s absence from a screen does not demonstrate complete revocation. Every result is bound to a date, policy revision and acceptance condition; support notes retain a status distinct from technical verification.

machine_specs.summary: Document custody links the original, revision, acceptance, thumbnail and download. The analysis focuses on propagating policy to every derivative.

phases.name: Object and derivative inventory
phases.narrative: Document D1 produces a thumbnail, search excerpt, temporary export and deliverable annex. Each derivative retains a reference to its source, revision and classification. The notebook requires an inventory of consumers before claiming complete withdrawal because their naming conventions may differ from the main file’s.

phases.name: Purpose and revision-specific access
phases.narrative: The recipient receives only revisions permitted by its mandate. Reclassification or removal of a participant changes download authorization even if the link has not expired. Acceptance compares an authorized document with another whose permission has been withdrawn; the reserved destination is never queried.

phases.name: Acceptance of immutable content
phases.narrative: The approved case file contains a component manifest. Replacing an annex with different bytes under the same name changes its revision and requires new acceptance. The model’s signature is a documentary relationship, not a real electronic signature or proof of a person’s identity.

phases.name: Withdrawal and retention
phases.narrative: Removal propagates to the original, thumbnail, index and temporary copy. The notebook distinguishes logical access withdrawal, removal of a reference and physical deletion. A verification limitation remains visible rather than being replaced by a count of deleted rows in the main catalog.

phases.name: Publication and limitations
phases.narrative: Delivery uses reviewed derivatives, while the editable project may retain the private original. Known markers help detect specific leaks, but their absence does not establish universal privacy. Scanned images, semantic context and out-of-scope content require explicitly identified additional review.

machine_specs.summary: The delivery chain represents artifacts, configuration and promotion. This notebook uses inert packages and neither builds nor executes software for the fictional bank.

phases.name: Approved-input inventory
phases.narrative: The manifest identifies source, dependencies, configuration and artifact by revision and hash. Provenance is not reduced to a pipeline-run name. When an earlier result is reused, the record retains that relationship and explains why it remains valid for the current inputs.

phases.name: Separating review from publication
phases.narrative: The review phase has permission only to read inputs and publish validation results. Promotion uses a different identity limited to an approved artifact. The notebook compares effective permissions in both phases and records rejection of a write outside the review function.

phases.name: Identity of the delivered assembly
phases.narrative: An approved binary does not automatically cover configuration added afterward. Acceptance compares the final assembly against the manifest, including relevant destinations and policies. Files with the same name and different content must produce an explicit discrepancy that blocks partial promotion.

phases.name: Rollback under current restrictions
phases.narrative: The earlier version may contain a retired dependency or permission. Before using it as a fallback, current restrictions are applied and a compatible package is prepared. Rollback is treated as a new delivery with its own review, without assuming that stability in the past means acceptability today.

phases.name: Closure and provenance evidence
phases.narrative: Evidence binds the result of each control to the hash that would be promoted. Neither reproducibility of a real system nor universal absence of dead code is claimed. Test components and examples are retained when their consumers are demonstrated; removal is limited to items whose lack of use can be justified.

machine_specs.summary: The corporate directory models groups, inheritance and delegations. It contains no real domain names, credentials or access to identity services.

phases.name: Effective-authority inventory
phases.narrative: Direct, inherited and transitive permissions over objects and groups are listed. An inventory role can read attributes without gaining the ability to change members or owners. The matrix records who delegated each right and which administrative boundary it effectively reaches.

phases.name: Separation of administrative duties
phases.narrative: The model distinguishes a service account, a backup operator and an interactive administrator. Sharing a credential across functions broadens its authority and makes decisions harder to attribute. The notebook retains read, declared-task and interactive-session rejection cases for every relevant identity.

phases.name: Group withdrawal and sessions
phases.narrative: Changing the group catalog does not necessarily update existing sessions. The scenario withdraws a delegation and compares an earlier session with a new one. Both must converge on current permissions, or the outcome must explicitly identify the consumer that has not yet applied the policy.

phases.name: Recovery of structure and permissions
phases.narrative: A directory backup may predate removal of a group or its owner. Recovery incorporates a record of later changes and checks both allowed access and rejected modifications. Restored content is not accepted merely because its structure can be read.

phases.name: Closure with limitations
phases.narrative: The outcome documents the objects, operations and revisions considered. A group check is not extrapolated to the entire directory. Temporary exceptions retain an owner and expiry; support permissions are reviewed without turning a monitoring need into permanent administration.

machine_specs.summary: The continuity orchestrator coordinates backups, ledger, queues and write authority. Its phases describe an isolated conceptual exercise.

phases.name: Reopening-dependency inventory
phases.narrative: Backup C1 includes objects and policies from a specific date. The catalog links manifest, ledger, queue, identity and configuration. Each dependency declares whether it can be recovered independently and which revision it needs before accepting operations. Missing components remain visible blockers.

phases.name: Integrity and completeness
phases.narrative: The exercise compares names, sizes and hashes of all required members. A restored index does not establish that its objects exist or share the same revision. The documentation covers a complete backup, one with a missing member and another with substituted content under the same name.

phases.name: State and revocation reconciliation
phases.narrative: Before reopening, completed obligations are compared with pending messages. Revocations and reclassifications made after the backup are also applied. The scenario requires a retired supplier to remain without access and an already cleared obligation to produce no new effect.

phases.name: Write authority and failover
phases.narrative: The alternate node receives a versioned write grant that invalidates the earlier one. The old primary must reject changes under its expired grant even if it does not immediately observe the replacement’s activation. Acceptance evaluates effective authority, not merely the availability of both processes.

phases.name: Reopening decision
phases.narrative: The reopening decision lists satisfied, partial and blocked criteria. The fictional owner may restrict the service to a verified flow, but that decision does not make the remainder recovered. Evidence retains revision, date and scope and distinguishes backup creation from accepted restoration.

machine_specs.summary: Fraud monitoring represents data, models and explainable decisions. It neither evaluates people nor measures the commercial accuracy or bias of a real model.

phases.name: Data and contract inventory
phases.narrative: Each input retains source, unit, currency, schema and sequence. The notebook includes a complete batch, one with a missing field and another with a different scale. Acceptance requires more than file validity: the consumer must understand the meaning of its numbers.

phases.name: Model and threshold identity
phases.narrative: The decision retains an immutable model version, parameters and threshold. A reusable label is insufficient to reconstruct the result. Model M1 and its successor M2 retain separate records so a later review does not attribute the behavior of subsequently published parameters to M1.

phases.name: Late data and reprocessing
phases.narrative: An older revision is retained as a late event and does not silently replace current state. Reprocessing distinguishes correction of an input from repetition of that same input. The result must identify which decisions were reviewed and avoid duplicating events merely because the batch was read again.

phases.name: Indicators and denominators
phases.narrative: The example separates received, accepted, rejected and pending items. An unknown field does not become zero, and every percentage identifies its base. Executive presentation preserves the same limitations as technical detail so visual simplification does not turn missing data into an absence of events.

phases.name: Closure and explainability
phases.narrative: The notebook binds each output to the data and model contract that produced it. It does not claim that a documentary explanation guarantees model correctness. Fictional results exercise continuity of tables, references and retests; any decision about a real system would require independent evidence.
